**Participants:** Wren Duskfield (Ops Lead)

Wren: "Every new hire completes the Pallasine checklist in their first

old wiki page last quarter."

positions.name: PallasineChecklistAsCurrentStandard
positions.frame: what establishes the Pallasine checklist as the legitimate, current onboarding standard?
positions.why: Both expressions come from the same speaker in the same breath describing the same artifact, and both read in the authority/legitimacy direction the relational and power observations flag: src-1 states the checklist as a universal mandate ('every new hire completes'), src-2 grounds that mandate's legitimacy in supersession ('replaced the old wiki page last quarter'). Together they cohere as one claim about what makes this the operative process now — content (what it requires) plus provenance (what it displaced) — rather than two independent facts. No tension to narrate; the two facets reinforce a single institutional-legitimacy read.

placements.why: Onboarding — new-hire process, checklist, accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift — is organizational-operations content: how the org runs itself internally, not opportunity, strategy, product, architecture, proof, template, or calibration material. No strata exists yet in this repo, and nothing supplied is even close, so this is the NEW case: mint the top-level category the content itself names, standalone, no forced parent.

placements.why: Both segments describe the same subject — the new-hire onboarding sequence — as an ongoing organizational practice future envelopes will keep feeding: src-1 states its current required components (checklist, accounts, pairing rotation, shadow shift) as a standing rule ('every new hire completes'), src-2 supplies the artifact's own history (superseding the prior wiki page). This passes the narrative grain test — it names a subject that persists and accrues, not a one-time measurement — so both segments are evidence for one onboarding-process leaf rather than a leaf for the 'replaced the wiki' fact itself. No existing leaf or strata (both empty for this repo) plausibly holds it, and nothing supplied is close enough to justify an INSPIRED lineage edge, so this is a standalone NEW mint nested under the newly minted Organization stratum.
